content: Diabetes UK is a British charity that focuses on supporting patients, healthcare professionals, and researchers in the field of diabetes. Its mission is to improve the lives of individuals living with diabetes and to work towards a future free from this chronic condition. The organization was established in 1934 under the name The Diabetic Association by H.G. Wells and Dr. R.D. Lawrence. It underwent two name changes: in 1954, it became The British Diabetic Association, and in 2000, it was renamed Diabetes UK. The charity maintains a website that provides comprehensive information about diabetes for both healthcare professionals and individuals living with the condition. Diabetes UK has a membership base exceeding 180,000, which includes people with diabetes, their caregivers, and healthcare professionals. The first voluntary group of the organization was formed in 1939, and today, there are approximately 350 such groups across the UK. Additionally, the charity operates local offices throughout England and national offices in Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales. It organizes conferences for its volunteers and healthcare professionals specializing in diabetes care. The charity actively campaigns for advancements in the care and treatment of individuals with diabetes. Since the 1930s, it has been running care holidays for children with diabetes, and over time, it has expanded to include holidays for families and adults. These holidays are designed to offer support and advice in a relaxed and enjoyable environment. In 1993, Diabetes UK launched a counseling service called Careline, which provides support to patients, their families, and friends. This service can be accessed via a low-cost phone number, email, or post. The organization also maintains an internal library and offers a science inquiry service. Diabetes UK funds research within the UK to investigate the causes, treatments, and complications of diabetes. The first research grant was awarded in 1936. The charity produces a variety of informational booklets and magazines, including Balance, which is aimed at patients. This magazine was originally called The Diabetic Journal when it was first published in 1935, and it was renamed Balance in 1961. For healthcare professionals, the charity publishes Diabetes Update. Additionally, Diabetes UK collaborates with Blackwell Publishing to produce the academic journal Diabetic Medicine. Earlier issues of this journal, from Volume 1 in 1984 to Volume 17 in mid-2000, were published by John Wiley and Sons.
